The Senior Advanced Manufacturing Engineer (AME) for Plastics is knowledgeable in injection mold tooling and processing, molding equipment, and plastics part design. This role involves managing tooling and equipment projects by executing necessary activities at each milestone throughout the project. The Senior AME plays a pivotal role in guiding and mentoring entry level AMEs within the team on how to manage and execute projects.

This role also serves as a lead technical/engineering liaison for the Center of Excellence (COE), which is the internal plastics “supplier” of all Appliance Park in-house molded products.

Position
Senior Advanced Manufacturing Engineer – Plastics

Location
USA, Louisville, KY

How You'll Create Possibilities

Manufacturing Project Management:

· Provides technical COE guidance for all processes, cross-functional team meetings, and design reviews for injection molds, injection molding presses and associated automation equipment

· Support the GE Appliances Business Change Request (BCR) process

· Take a lead role managing multiple simultaneous projects

· Develop technical specifications to ensure accurate and timely delivery of associated molds/equipment

· Ensure Equipment Qualification projects are accurately created in Oracle Agile as the primary AME project management process

· Drive projects through each milestone completion with necessary stakeholder engagement and ensure Agile is updated in a timely manner

· Ability to manage and report on capital spending, project timeline/delivery status and other KPI related aspects of a project

Safety, Quality, Productivity, Cost:

· Maintain certified Lock Out (LOTO) status for safe equipment operation

· Lead supplier Risk Assessment review and EHS approvals of all applicable equipment

· Provide guidance on part dimensional and tolerance requirements to ensure Design for Manufacturability (DFM)

· Join Cross-functional teams to resolve part design or equipment requirement issues

· Collaborate with Plastics CAE experts to analyze design, quality and productivity related aspects of new plastic part designs

· Lead RFQ process for quotes, summarize and recommend suppliers to achieve low cost, on time results

· Track supplier delivery and provide accountability to avoid timeline delays

· Provide communication within the COE team to ensure smooth plant implementation of molds and equipment

What You'll Bring to Our Team

Minimum Requirements:

· Ability to collaborate effectively across multiple levels of the organization to promote operational success and continuous improvement

· High energy, initiative, and motivation to contribute to a team-oriented environment

· Organizational skills with the ability to manage simultaneous projects and tasks efficiently

· Strong problem-solving abilities and follow-through on initiatives

Minimum Qualifications:

· 5+ years of experience in injection molding or manufacturing engineering

· Experience with injection molding equipment, resin delivery systems, robotic part load/unload systems, and injection mold troubleshooting

· Equipment procurement experience (quoting, sourcing, implementation)

· Project Management experience in a cross-functional manufacturing environment

Preferred Qualifications:

· Bachelor of Science in Engineering degree (plastics / mechanical / manufacturing engineering / industrial / electrical)

· Hands-on experience in injection molding part/mold design, molding machines and/or automated equipment operations

· Moldflow/Moldex CAE working knowledge

· CAD experience

· RJG injection molding knowledge

· Sepro and/or Fanuc Robotics experience

· Working conditions are normal for both an office and manufacturing environments.

· Work may involve lifting materials and products up to 25 pounds.

· Working in the manufacturing environment requires the use of safety equipment to include but not limited to safety glasses, hearing protection, gloves, work shoes/boots.

This role will interact heavily with Factory Operations, Technology, Supplier Quality, Sourcing, and Advanced Manufacturing. Position
Advanced Manufacturing Engineer – Finishes COE

Location
USA, Louisville, KY

• Interface with coating suppliers, applicators, and manufacturing sites to improve coatings initiatives for the business.

• Identify new coating’s processes, tools, and contacts within the industry – including new suppliers, instruments, or processes to further advance the business.

• Utilize the Finishes Execution Scorecard, Technical Audits, and other quality tools to identify and drive quality projects across all coatings operations resulting in the overall improvement of Premium Finishes at GEA.

• Monitor and resolve coatings process control performance issues by adhering to quality control plans and implementing sustainable corrective actions

• Drive permanent resolution of coatings and finishes Cost of Quality issues caused by manufacturing and supplier defects.

• Lead projects involving coatings supplier moves, process and material changes.  Support design change projects.

• Support the GEA finishes commercial strategy through qualification of alternate suppliers and materials, data collection of current process state, and integration with the operations and equipment requirements.

• Lead problem definition and reactive problem solving of coatings issues through disciplined root cause and corrective action.

• Provide clear and concise project status updates to leadership teams.

• Identify areas for cost reduction within coatings and finishing processes both internal and external.

• Engineering or Technical degree (Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics) or equivalent technical experience

• Minimum 2 years Advanced Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, and/or Technical experience in manufacturing environment

• Understanding of statistical tools for process and product development and control (i.e. Gage R&R, Process Capability, Control Plans, SPC, Process Failure Mode Effects Analysis (PFMEA) and Design of Experiments (DOEs)).

• Understanding of with problem solving tools and component qualification (i.e., 8-D, 5 Whys, 7 Ways, DOE, eCAR, Fishbone, Pareto, Six Sigma, First Piece, PPAP).

The Veteran Development Program is a unique opportunity for experienced Navy, Marine, Army or Air Force, Coast Guard, and Space Force commissioned officers to work a 2-year rotational program in Louisville, KY, Decatur, AL, or LaFayette, GA. Qualified candidates are selected to start their careers in a 2 year, cross-functional, rotational training program, which includes both on-the-job and formal classroom training. The program is focused on providing a broad range of useful experience while cultivating the skills you will need to enjoy a successful career.

As a participant in this program, you may perform your rotations in several functional business areas, primarily in manufacturing, operations and supply chain. Through these exceptional rotational opportunities, this program provides you with broad business experience and exposure to the various core systems that make up GE Appliances.

Position
Veteran Development Program

Location
USA, Louisville, KY

How You'll Create Possibilities

You'll interact with senior-level technical and business heads, and you'll receive valuable mentoring and coaching that foster personal development. Rotational assignments provide valuable contacts and experience that accelerate the development of your technical, business and professional skills for your first role in manufacturing or operations.

• Successfully complete a 2-year rotational assignment in different areas of the supply chain organization including: manufacturing operations leadership roles, sourcing/purchasing, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, manufacturing engineering, materials and material flow, and Lean.

• Set goals & targets for your rotation with your assignment lead.

• Lead teams across multiple levels of the business through influencing.

• Use initiative to find and develop process improvements.

• Assist your team with the development and execution of project ideas.

• Develop and demonstrate a systematic approach to problem-solving.

• Demonstrate the ability to work autonomously.

• Set regular feedback sessions with your assignment lead.

• Participate in and complete classroom-based leadership and functional training as well as online training curriculum.

What You'll Bring to Our Team

Requirements:

• Bachelor's degree required

• Achieved a military grade of E6 or higher OR is a Commissioned Officer

• Maximum of 2 years of separation from active duty; exceptions may apply for candidates with full-time enrollment in higher education or relevant experience in manufacturing or supply chain within the 2-year period

• Exceptional military career as demonstrated through successful completion of leadership and key developmental assignments

• Ability to solve problems, delegate, and achieve difficult goals

• Ability to adapt quickly and eager to learn and master new roles

• Demonstrated passion for supply chain and/or manufacturing

• Methodical approach to problem-solving

• Exceptional interpersonal skills and leadership skills

• Excellent oral and written communication skills

The successful candidate will have a strong understanding of GEA’s people, processes, and NPI environment and will be responsible for connecting product design requirements with manufacturing capability. The role will lead cross-functional teams to deliver turn-key, sustainable solutions that meet quality requirements at launch and enable manufacturing teams to confidently take ownership of production execution.

This position will also drive the advancement of GEA’s metrology and dimensional analysis capabilities, including ADS, GD&T, scanning technologies, CMMs, portable measurement systems, PolyWorks, Dataloop, and related digital quality tools.

Position

Location
USA, Louisville, KY

How You'll Create Possibilities

New Product Introduction (NPI)

• Provide metrology and dimensional quality leadership throughout the NPI process, from initial product development through production launch.

• Partner with cross-functional teams to implement new parts, products, and processes that are turn-key, sustainable, and production-ready at launch.

• Ensure manufacturing teams agree to and can effectively assume ownership of measurement and quality processes at production launch.

• Lead the launch of new products and features with measurable improvements in Cost of Quality (COQ) compared with current production.

• Lead cross-functional efforts to integrate the Measurement System Alignment process into the iNPI process.

• Develop, publish, and release draft Standard Instructions (SIs) for equipment qualification.

• Create and maintain GEA metrology standards and update iNPI and C-change checklists to strengthen measurement-system requirements.

• Lead metrology work-order meetings across GEA product lines and identify opportunities to improve process effectiveness, responsiveness, and quality.

• Serve as the bridge between Product Design and Manufacturing to ensure dimensional and measurement issues are identified and resolved early, minimizing launch surprises.

• Provide technical leadership and in-depth expertise in the investigation, development, procurement, qualification, and implementation of manufacturing equipment and processes.

• Work effectively with salaried and hourly personnel to understand operator needs, program requirements, and business objectives.

Current Production Support

• Apply the same metrology, dimensional quality, and process-improvement leadership used in NPI to current-production and new-part/product PCTO-related projects introduced at CIB.

• Develop robust processes for reviewing production measurement data and use the results to drive improved product drawings, specifications, and manufacturing processes.

At GE Appliances, a Haier company, we come together to make “good things, for life.”  As the fastest-growing appliance company in the U.S., we’re powered by creators, thinkers and makers who believe that anything is possible and that there’s always a better way.  We believe in the power of our people and in giving them the freedom to explore, discover and build good things, together.

The GE Appliances philosophy, backed by three simple commitments defines the way we work, invent, create, do business, and serve our communities: we come together, we always look for a better way, and we create possibilities.

Interested in joining us on our journey?

Join Bodewell, the official service team of GE Appliances, and become more than a technician; be a trusted advisor, a customer hero, and a brand ambassador for a company that’s redefining service excellence.

As an Appliance Care Expert, you’ll combine hands-on repair skills with the power to deliver smart, lasting solutions. From repairing major household appliances to confidently recommending service plans and accessories, your role is equal parts technician, educator, and representative of a brand customers trust. If you love solving problems, helping people, and building a career with purpose we want to hear from you.
If you can fix it, and show the value in protecting it, you’ll thrive here.

At GE Appliances, we put our people first, and that includes you. Here’s what you can expect as part of the Bodewell team:

• Annual wage increases and uncapped incentive opportunities
• Service van provided
• Laptop computer and smartphone
• Uniforms, work boots, and specialized tools
• Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance on DAY ONE
• 401K and tuition reimbursement
• Paid vacation and paid holidays
• Career growth opportunities and continuous technical training

Competitive hourly rates: $23 – $32+ base, depending on experience, certifications, and location.

Position
Appliance Service Technician (Gulf Shores, AL)

Location
USA, Mobile, AL

How You'll Create Possibilities

As a Bodewell Appliance Care Technician, your responsibilities will include:

• Diagnosing and completing in-home repairs on GE Appliances' major appliances

• Using sound judgment to recommend repair vs replacement based on cost-effectiveness and customer needs, prioritizing repairs whenever practical.

• Promoting and selling service contracts, water filters, and related products/appliances as appropriate, always focusing on value-driven solutions and the best customer experience

• Operating an assigned Bodewell service van to customer locations

• Accurately documenting repairs, routes, and work activities

• Participating in training sessions, meetings, and events to maintain industry expertise

• Managing inventory and maintenance of your service vehicle

• Delivering high-quality service and maintaining strong customer satisfaction

• Following all safety protocols to protect yourself and others

What You'll Bring to Our Team

Minimum Qualifications:

• HS Diploma or General Education Degree (GED)

• 1+ years of experience with appliance repair, electrical, mechanical, HVAC, or property maintenance

• Ability/experience diagnosing and repairing major appliances

• Excellent customer service and communication skills with a responsive, professional approach.

• Basic computer aptitude including proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite specifically Microsoft Outlook and Microsoft Teams.

• Ability to work a flexible schedule with some Saturdays as needed

• Have and maintain a valid state driver's license and successfully complete background check, physical, and drug screen.

• Must have or be willing to obtain CFC Certification within 6 months.

• Wear uniform & maintain standards of personal grooming & appearance consistent with GE Appliance values

• Self-directed and solid team player

• Ability to deescalate situations and rebuild customer confidence in our products

• Ability to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without accommodation, including, but not limited to:

• Ability to step up, into, and out of a van and sit for extended periods of time

• Ability to handle/work with parts/equipment which may be hot, cold, and/or wet

• Ability to use often powered hand tools and occasional use of vibratory tools/equipment

• Ability to handle and lift parts or materials min. of 77 lbs. lifting/carrying and 70 lb. pushing/pulling is required

Preferred Qualifications:

• 6 plus months of experience with Refrigeration repair

• Experience using Salesforce or similar customer relationship management (CRM) systems.

• CFC Certified

• Certification in appliance repair or associate’s degree preferred

• Read and interpret wiring diagrams, schematics and other service information.

Our Culture

Our work is centered on our People and Culture as reflected in our Zero Distance philosophy and we recognize the importance of reaffirming our commitment to inclusion and diversity (I&D). This underscores our commitment to fostering an environment where every individual feels valued, connected, and empowered to contribute, while positioning our organization to adapt seamlessly to the evolving needs of our workforce and communities.

This reflects our dedication to creating solutions that: Empower colleagues by fostering an environment where all voices are heard, valued, and encouraged to contribute. Strengthen communities where we live and work. Reinforce a culture of belonging, purpose, and engagement. Reflect the diversity of the communities we serve through our workforce, products, and practices.

By further embedding Zero Distance into our People and Culture framework, we will continue to build a deeply connected organization. We are cultivating a culture of engagement, belonging, and connection, because while attracting new talent remains a priority, retention is a cornerstone of our strategy.

GE Appliances is a trust-based organization. It is important we offer our employees the flexibility they need to do their best work while balancing the needs of the business and individuals. When you join GE Appliances, you will have the opportunity to work with your leader to create a flexible work arrangement that balances the needs of the individual, team, and organization.

GE Appliances is an Equal Opportunity Employer.  Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

description:
At GE Appliances, a Haier company, we come together to make “good things, for life.”  As the fastest-growing appliance company in the U.S., we’re powered by creators, thinkers and makers who believe that anything is possible and that there’s always a better way.  We believe in the power of our people and in giving them the freedom to explore, discover and build good things, together.

The GE Appliances philosophy, backed by three simple commitments defines the way we work, invent, create, do business, and serve our communities: we come together, we always look for a better way, and we create possibilities.

Interested in joining us on our journey?

The Principal Advanced Manufacturing Engineer (AME) is a member of a product line AME team responsible for providing manufacturing support New Product Introduction (NPI), Cost-Out and Plant Productivity projects. The AME shall develop, manage and execute capital equipment and high-volume manufacturing process projects to meet the required budget and launch schedules. The AME is a key liaison between NPI programs and the factory operations teams; ensuring plant priorities and objectives are clearly understood and considered. This includes providing input for design for manufacturability, applying lean principles to process designs and transferring process knowledge to the applicable factory personnel. The role requires strong experience with manufacturing equipment and automation systems used in high-volume production environments as well as Openness to leveraging AI-assisted tools and technologies to support technical documentation creation, review, process standardization, and knowledge management activities.

Position
Principal Advanced Manufacturing Engineer

Location
USA, Louisville, KY

How You'll Create Possibilities

Technical Responsibilities:

•
Coordinate and manage capital equipment procurement projects: Including specification development utilizing GE Appliances & industry standards, supplier selection, early supplier engagement, technical reviews, factory layout development, installation and qualification of equipment.  Ensure all tooling and equipment is reliable and robust and designed to maximize Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE).

•
Own the program metrics as applicable to your assigned projects: capital equipment & tooling budgets, program schedule, reliability, quality and labor targets.  Work with the program team to perform trade-off analysis on competing metrics if necessary and drive decisions based on overall business impact.

•
Facilitate/lead the use of the Production Preparation Process (3P) and Lean manufacturing principles while developing manufacturing equipment and processes.  Utilize cross-functional participation to ensure that the equipment and processes are compatible with the entire value stream.  Efforts should include right-sized equipment, workstation design, material presentation, standard work and single piece flow.

•
Demonstrated willingness to embrace emerging digital technologies, including AI-assisted tools, to improve engineering documentation, process development, project execution, and collaboration efficiency.

Standards and Compliance:

•
Ensure all equipment executed in GEA factories comply with Industry and Governmental Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) standards.

•
Utilize Human Organizational Performance (HOP) principles to ensure that all equipment / tooling / processes are implemented with the health and safety of the operators in mind.

•
Work with functional leaders to ensure equipment & processes support business initiatives of Bill of Process (BoP), Lean Manufacturing, Ergonomic Design and Total Productive Maintenance (TPM)

Cross-functional Work and Leadership:

•
Work with factory operations and Lean teams to understand Value Stream and how your projects impact this.  Ensure material flow, workstation set up, model mix, etc. are considered when workstations / equipment is designed.

•
Utilize the 9-Step Process for tooling and equipment design; consult Critical Process leaders as applicable to ensure development of robust processes for part / product generation.  Work with cross-functional team to develop Manufacturing Control Plans (MCP) and Manufacturing Control Instructions (MCI).

•
Work with the design team to ensure Design for Manufacturing & Assembly (DFMA) is considered part design.

•
As a Principal AME, participate in growing the AME organization’s capability.  This includes mentoring, guiding and helping more junior team members as well as adding to the body of knowledge of the department (training, developing new manufacturing processes, supporting Hoshin objectives, etc.)

What You'll Bring to Our Team

Minimum Requirements:

•
Bachelor of Science Degree in Engineering or related discipline OR equivalent hands-on experience in technical/manufacturing disciplines

•
7+ years of hands-on experience in manufacturing equipment and processes.

Preferred Skills:

•
Proficiency in AutoCAD

•
Prior involvement in New Product Introduction (NPI) programs

•
Proven success in managing capital equipment projects, including supplier selection, installation, and qualification.

•
Experience applying Lean manufacturing principles.

•
Strong communication and leadership skills to engage with diverse teams, from shop floor operators to senior management.

Travel:

•

The Senior Manufacturing Quality Engineer – Test Systems is responsible for managing the quality test manufacturing systems, test loops and final product testing. Position
Test Engineer - Manufacturing Quality

Location
USA, Louisville, KY

New Product Introduction

• Develop and implement new and improved test methods to enhance capabilities, support growth, new model introduction, and improve outgoing quality via enhanced test firewalls.

• Drive improvement projects through the CIB process.  i.e. Able to write and analyze Test Codes for leak and flow rates, wattage, resistance, Hipot, Ground bond and other basic test parameters.

• Drive project improvement pulsing’s including organizing project leaders around Test Systems improvement goals.

Error Proofing

• Implement Poke-Yoke work methods for testing and develop standard work and workstation aids to assist in operator training and operational consistency to improve quality yields.

• Review daily assembly line test loops for equipment failure. Work with Process Improvement Engineers and maintenance to have the equipment repaired.

Factory Support

• Provide first response to Business Team leader regarding production related issues surrounding test equipment.

• Drive to maintain a partnership with our shop operations personnel to promote a team that reacts aggressively to factory inefficiencies.

Sustain

• Experience in the function of basic electrical components

• Demonstrated ability to drive continuous improvement in a manufacturing environment, influencing others and driving change

• Computer literate and skilled in Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Minitab, and Outlook

• Electrical System Testing

• Program C++

• Low Voltage Start

The GE Appliances Tooling Engineer - Metals will be a member of the Metal Stamping Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) team. The Metal Stamping AME Team owns and maintains the engineering standards for metal stamping tooling and equipment for the company. The engineer will be responsible for assisting and supporting the management and execution of tooling and metal stamping equipment projects, helping to ensure that all tooling and equipment are compliant with standards and executed within the project or program deliverables (safety, cost, quality and delivery). At times, the engineer will be assigned to New Product Introduction (NPI) programs or to product lines projects to drive product cost out and factory productivity. USA, Louisville, KY

Monogram General Factory Operator

Location
USA, Selmer, TN

• Maintain basic housekeeping including sweeping and use of electronic cleaning equipment.

• Follow standard work. Complete tasks within takt time.

• Ability to work in loud or noisy environment.

• Perform associated and other duties as required.

• High school diploma or equivalent required.

• Must be 18 years of age or older.

• Must be legally authorized to work in the US

• Must read, write, and follow written instructions.

• Must be able to perform duties within a prescribed time limit as well as wear safety glasses and observe all safety rules.

Handling, lifting, and carrying parts/equipment (maximum 54 lbs. and pushing/pulling 20 lbf.). Requires working with chemicals. Requires tolerance to heights in excess of six (6) feet and to noise levels between 70 to 90 dba.

• Preferred: one year assembly manufacturing experience OR three months successful experience manufacturing refrigerators OR Certified Production Technician Certificate.

Location
USA, Selmer, TN

• Lead off shift Sheet Metal Teams at multiple facilities

• Responsible for operational performance and improvement of key metrics including safety, quality, delivery, cost and morale. Align area metrics with overall department/value stream goals; organize resources to deliver on these metrics.

• Work cross-functionally with multiple stakeholders to solve quality issues (i.e. Team Leader, engineering, quality).

• Identify critical processes where manufacturing control plans will be required and ensure they are adequately documented, manufacturing site supports, and they are implemented into production.

• Drive awareness and utilization of Proactive Quality Tools (error proofing, pokey-yoke, line interlocks) to maximize impact on ongoing operations.

CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT:

Live, promote and teach the Appliance Production System philosophy and drive continuous improvement within assigned production area.

• Communicate key issues to leadership team.

• Support and maintain the standardized work within the production area.

• Train all employees on the Job Instruction method by reviewing and verifying Job Instruction   forms, including cross training matrix.

• Support the team leaders to sustain the 5S standards are being met for the area.

• Support the Business Leader in managing a cross-functional team (PIE’s, Team Leaders, Kaizen Promotion Officers and other Lean resources) to continuously identify and work to reduce waste in the area for both short term and long-term improvement initiatives.

• Participate in meetings to review department issues. Assist in prioritizing and assigning ownership for open items in assigned production area. Track items to closure and ensure follow-up with key stakeholders.

• Participate in the planning and execution of work area rebalancing utilizing Yamazumi charts.

LEADERSHIP & ADMINISTRATION:                                                                                                                                                           Provide active day-to-day leadership, work direction and support for a manufacturing team within a production area.

• Partner with site Human Resources team to ensure fair and consistent administration of all policies, work rules and processes.

• Oversee line staffing and allocate employees to cover absenteeism.

• Complete job postings as needed.

• Complete timecards daily and ensure employees receive appropriate pay for time worked. Ensure upgrades are properly coded, leave types are identified and overtime is properly calculated.

• Identify and communicate Overtime needs.  When applicable, acquire overtime help and accurately apply overtime guidelines..

• Partner with HR to conduct timely investigations when necessary. Complete accurate and thorough disciplinary records with supporting documentation.

• Ensure attendance discipline is issued in a timely manner and consistent with the Attendance Policy.

• Distribute written communications in a timely fashion.

• Ensure all quality processes/standards are followed within assigned production area.

• Monitor quality issues on a daily basis and drives the resolution or escalation for any defect.

• Ensure Team Leaders include quality standards in Standardized Work to meet design intent and build in quality.

• Work cross-functionally with multiple stakeholders to address and solve production line quality issues (i.e. Team Leader, engineering, quality).

• Monitor scrap data/reports to drive resolution of scrap issues and work projects to prevent future scrap.

• Partner with Plant Quality and Engineering staff to drive improvements in First Pass Yield and Service Call Rate (SCR) metrics.

SAFETY:

Responsible for the safety performance and metrics for the production area.

Safety is everyone’s responsibility, Promote safety culture and ensure all sheet metal teams are compliance with safety rules and procedures, such as: PPE compliance, accident investigation within 24 hours, Safety Contacts and safe start participation. Support facility security during the off-shift hours

Position Requirement

• Demonstrated experience working with individuals at all levels of the organization to achieve operational results and positive employee relations.

• High level of initiative, energy and motivation to develop & grow in a team environment.

• Organizational skills, initiative, and ability to handle multiple priorities and tasks.

• Strong technical competency & experience.

• Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills.

• Strong problem-solving & follow-through ability.

• Ability to facilitate team projects.

• Position supports 24/5 manufacturing facilities. Occasional overtime, l and weekend work required.

• Leadership/management experience and/or equivalent technical acumen within a manufacturing operation.

Preferred Qualifications:

• 5 years of leadership experience and project implementation.

• Preferred, Six Sigma certification with strong knowledge of Lean

• Demonstrated accomplishments showing results-driven methodology, analytical methods, schedule achievement, teamwork.

The ME will also be a key liaison between NPI programs and the plant operations teams; ensuring that plant priorities and objectives are clearly understood and considered for the area under their ownership.

Position
Manufacturing Engineer

Location
USA, Selmer, TN

How You'll Create Possibilities

• Manage specification development utilizing GE standards, supplier selection, early supplier engagement, technical reviews, factory layout development, installation and qualification of equipment.

• Ensure all tooling and equipment is reliable and robust and designed to maximize Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE).

• Own the program metrics as applicable to your assigned projects: manufacturing labor plan (VLOH), equipment and tooling budgets and quality of in-house manufactured parts/product. Efforts should include: Part and Process cross functional activities, early equipment management (TPM), workstation design, material presentation, standard work and single piece flow. Work with cross-functional team to develop Manufacturing Control Plans (MCP) and Manufacturing Control Instructions (MCI).

• Work with Advanced Manufacturing Engineering, EHS and the Advanced Industrial Engineer equipment / tooling / processes are implemented with the health and safety of the operators in mind.

• Work with factory operations and Lean teams to understand the Value Stream and how your projects impact this. Ensure material flow, workstation setup, model mix, Design for Manufacturing & Assembly (DFMA), etc. are considered when workstations / equipment is designed.

What You'll Bring to Our Team

• Technical Degree or equivalent

• Experience 2+ years hands on experience in manufacturing equipment and processes

Location
USA, LaFayette, GA

New Product Introduction & Launch

Equipment & Process Qualification

• Own and lead equipment and process qualification activities within the assigned area of responsibility.

• Qualify in-house equipment with minimal direction and ensure equipment is capable and ready for production use.

• Lead dimensional and process capability studies to validate equipment and process performance.

• Execute drive, strip, and torque studies on new joints to validate capability, performance, and process robustness.

• Identify opportunities to improve process capability, reduce variation, and establish sustainable manufacturing controls.

• Partner with equipment suppliers to resolve quality and capability issues prior to production launch.

Metrology & Measurement Systems

• Lead gage development for production, including specifications, design reviews, supplier coordination, and final buyoff.

• Facilitate gage kickoff meetings with AME, Plant Quality, Design Engineering, and other cross-functional stakeholders.

• Develop and maintain appropriate quality controls to prevent recurrence of manufacturing issues.

• Partner with Team Leaders and manufacturing teams to develop job instructions, define critical process requirements, and establish standard work.

• Develop and maintain Manufacturing Control Instructions (MCIs), Manufacturing Control Plans (MCPs), forms, and other required Quality Management System (QMS) documentation.

• Ensure process documentation and quality controls are established prior to production launch and maintained throughout the life of the process.

• Ensure applicable quality and process requirements are aligned with ISO standards and GEA quality systems.

• Support the transition of new processes and equipment from Advanced Manufacturing into sustainable plant operations.

• Provide technical guidance and mentorship to manufacturing and quality teams as needed.

• 2+ years of experience in Quality Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Process Engineering, or a similar technical role.

• Experience defining, implementing, troubleshooting, or improving manufacturing processes.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to use data to make sound technical decisions.

• Demonstrated ability to lead projects and influence cross-functional teams, including manufacturing and hourly production employees.

• Strong project management, planning, organization, and follow-through skills.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Experience with CMM, 3D scanning, metrology systems, or other dimensional measurement technologies.

• Experience programming and/or interpreting CMM and 3D scanning equipment.

• Experience with PolyWorks or similar dimensional analysis software.

• Experience with vision inspection systems, including Cognex or Keyence.

GE Appliances is seeking a Senior Security Engineer, Security Operations to serve as the senior technical lead for the company’s detection and response capability. Day-to-day 24x7 monitoring, alert triage, and vulnerability operations are delivered by our managed security services provider (MSSP); this role is not a shift lead or people manager. Instead, it owns the engineering behind the SOC — the detection and response platforms, detection content, automation, and telemetry — and drives the execution and continuous enhancement of how threats are detected, investigated, and contained across enterprise IT, cloud, and manufacturing (OT) environments. The engineer acts as the MSSP’s technical counterpart and the escalation point for complex incidents, and is accountable for measurable improvements in detection coverage, detection fidelity, and response speed.

Position
Senior Security Engineer- Security Operations

Location
USA, Louisville, KY

How You'll Create Possibilities

Key Responsibilities:

• Serve as the senior technical lead and subject-matter expert for security operations, owning the architecture, configuration, and operational health of the detection and response platforms and setting the technical standards the MSSP operates against.

• Design, build, test, and maintain detection content — correlation rules, behavioral analytics, and IOC/BIOC rules — mapped to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, and manage the full detection lifecycle using detection-as-code practices (version control, testing, peer review, and documentation).

• Own telemetry coverage: identify visibility gaps and onboard, parse, and normalize log sources across endpoints, identity, Microsoft 365, cloud, network, email, DLP, and OT; monitor ingestion health and manage data volume and retention cost.

• Engineer security automation and orchestration (SOAR) playbooks and integrations that enrich alerts, automate containment, and connect security tooling with IT service management and collaboration platforms to reduce manual effort and MSSP handling time.

• Provide technical oversight of MSSP output, in partnership with the Information Security leader who owns the MSSP commercial relationship: review triage and investigation quality, escalation accuracy, and run-book adherence; drive false-positive reduction and tuning; and update MSSP run books and playbooks as detections and the environment change.

• Serve as the Tier 3 escalation point and technical lead for complex or high-severity incidents escalated by the MSSP, performing hands-on investigation, endpoint and log analysis, scoping, and containment, and coordinating with the external incident response retainer when engaged.

• Lead hypothesis-driven threat hunting informed by threat intelligence and threats targeting manufacturing, converting hunt findings into durable detections and hardening recommendations.

• Operationalize threat intelligence by translating advisories, vulnerability disclosures, and adversary reporting into detections, hunts, and blocking actions, and track threat actors relevant to GE Appliances.

• Validate detection and response effectiveness through purple-team exercises, adversary emulation, and breach-and-attack simulation, measuring coverage against MITRE ATT&CK and confirming that the MSSP detects and responds as expected.

• Maintain EDR/XDR platform health across the endpoint and server estate, including agent coverage, prevention and exploit-protection policies, exclusions governance, and response actions.

• Strengthen the technical side of vulnerability operations run by the MSSP, including scan coverage and authenticated scanning, risk-based prioritization using exploitability and threat intelligence (e.g., CISA KEV, EPSS), correlation of vulnerabilities with active threat activity, and automation of remediation workflows.

• Partner with the Cloud, Network, and Identity security engineers to integrate cloud security posture (CNAPP), network, and identity signals into detection and response, including identity threat detection for account takeover, MFA fatigue, and adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) phishing.

• Partner with OT Security to extend monitoring and detection into manufacturing environments in a way that is safe for production and consistent with ISA/IEC 62443 and NIST SP 800-82.

• Author and maintain incident response playbooks, technical run books, and tabletop exercise scenarios, and lead the technical portion of post-incident reviews to drive corrective actions to closure.

• Define, automate, and report operational metrics and KPIs, such as MTTD, MTTR, ATT&CK detection coverage, false-positive rate, log source health, and MSSP escalation quality, to the CISO and Information Security leadership.

• Contribute to the security operations roadmap; evaluate emerging capabilities, including AI-assisted triage and investigation and agentic SOC automation; and support platform evaluations, proofs of concept, and total cost of ownership (TCO) analyses.

• Provide technical evidence for logging, monitoring, and incident response controls in SOX, C-SOX, PCI-DSS, and other audits, and drive remediation of related findings.

• Mentor engineers and transfer knowledge to MSSP analysts on the GE Appliances environment, detections, and response procedures.

What You'll Bring to Our Team

Requirements & Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

• 6–10 years of progressive experience in IT or information security, with at least 4+ years of hands-on experience in security operations, detection engineering, or incident response in a large enterprise environment.

• Deep hands-on experience engineering and administering SIEM/SOAR and EDR/XDR platforms (e.g., Palo Alto Networks Cortex XSIAM/XDR, Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel/Defender, CrowdStrike), including writing detection rules and queries (e.g., XQL, SPL, KQL).

• Proven experience building detection content mapped to MITRE ATT&CK and tuning it for fidelity at enterprise scale.

• Experience building SOAR playbooks and integrations, with proficiency in Python and/or PowerShell and working with REST APIs and JSON.

• Hands-on incident response experience with significant enterprise incidents such as ransomware, business email compromise (BEC), and account takeover, including endpoint, log, and network analysis.

• Experience working with an MSSP or MDR provider in a technical oversight role, including tuning, escalation quality review, and run-book development.

• Strong understanding of log sources and telemetry across Windows, Linux, network, cloud (AWS, Azure, and/or GCP), Microsoft 365, and identity providers.

• Working knowledge of frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, NIST SP 800-61 (incident handling), NIST CSF, and CIS Controls.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate with both technical and executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

• Certifications: GIAC (e.g., GCIH, GCIA, GCDA, GCFA, GCTI), Palo Alto Networks Cortex certifications, CISSP, or similar.

• Experience with detection-as-code practices, Git, CI/CD pipelines, and vendor-neutral rule formats such as Sigma.

• Experience with threat hunting, purple teaming, and adversary emulation tools (e.g., Atomic Red Team, MITRE Caldera, breach-and-attack simulation platforms).

• Familiarity with OT/ICS monitoring and frameworks such as ISA/IEC 62443 or NIST SP 800-82.

• Experience integrating cloud security (CNAPP/CSPM) and identity telemetry into detection and response.

• Identify and prioritize manufacturers, plumbing/HVAC distributors, contractor organizations, strategic sourcing customers, and adjacent channel partners with OEM, private label, or branded program needs.

• Build, manage, and continuously refine a qualified opportunity pipeline using market mapping, relationship development, proactive outreach, industry events, and referrals.

Interested in joining us on our journey?

GE Appliances Manager, Manufacturing Operations are frontline leaders responsible for overseeing manufacturing areas within a value stream. They lead, coach, and develop Team Leaders and hourly production team members to ensure high performance and continuous improvement in the areas of safety, quality, delivery and cost.

Position
Manager, Manufacturing Operations

Location
USA, Decatur, AL

How You'll Create Possibilities

MANUFACTURING OPERATIONS:  Provides support to the value stream Business Leader by leading the operational and improvement activities of an assigned production area within the value stream.

• Direct Reports include Team Leaders & Hourly Production team, members

• Responsible for operational performance and improvement of critical metrics including safety, quality, delivery, cost and morale. Align area metrics with overall department/value stream goals; organize resources to deliver on these metrics.

• Oversee the daily start-up of production area. Ensure line is properly staffed and manage staffing throughout the day; monitor expected and unexpected absenteeism. Review daily plan with Team Leaders.

• Ensure production line boards are completed in a timely manner. Utilize production line boards to collect information on area performance, issue identification and problem resolution. Ensure information is passed on to the following shift and management.

• Maintain a good technical knowledge of operations; follow the escalation process to address and respond to abnormalities and recommend corrective action as required.

• Act as a first responder to Team Leaders and production team members within the production area. Facilitate delegation of issues to appropriate level in escalation process.

• Ensure the Lean manufacturing practices and Escalation Process set forth under the Appliance Production System are followed and adhered to within the value stream manufacturing operations.

• Attend daily production meetings and cascade necessary information to Team Leaders. Lead and maintain rigor around daily Team Leader meetings, escalation meetings, etc. Communicate key issues to leadership team at the daily production meeting.

• Oversee the deployment of standardized work within the value stream operation. Ensure process stability through following standardized work. Coach and develop Team Leaders and team members to ensure standardized work is in place and is followed.

• Ensure adherence to Job Instruction method by reviewing and verifying Job Instruction forms, including cross training matrix, and Team Leader delivery of four step method to ensure ‘Critical Points’ and ‘Why’ are conveyed accurately and effectively.

• Ensure 5S standards are met for the area.

CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT:  Live, promote and teach the Appliance Production System philosophy and drive continuous improvement within assigned production area.

• Lead work team to react aggressively to factory inefficiencies. Drive problem-solving and root cause identification of problems for the production area. Engage all members of escalation team to address and resolve problems, ex. PIE, quality, facilities engineer, etc.

• Support the Business Leader in managing a cross-functional team (PIE’s, Team Leaders, Kaizen Promotion Officers and other Lean resources) to continuously identify and work to reduce waste in the area for both short term and long term improvement initiatives.

• Serve as a first responder within the escalation process for problems/issues within the value stream operation.

• Participate in meetings to review department issues. Assist in prioritizing and assigning ownership for open items in assigned production area. Track items to closure and ensure follow-up with key stakeholders.

• Champion kaizen events within department. Ensure related countermeasures are implemented on manufacturing line(s).

• Participate in the planning and execution of work area rebalancing utilizing Yamazumi charts.

LEADERSHIP & ADMINISTRATION:  Provide active day-to-day leadership, work direction and support for a manufacturing team within a production area.

• Partner with site Human Resources team to ensure fair and consistent administration of all policies, work rules and processes.

• Oversee line staffing and allocate employees to cover absenteeism.

• Complete job postings as needed.

• Complete timecards daily and ensure employees receive appropriate pay for time worked. Ensure upgrades are properly coded, leave types are identified and overtime is properly calculated.

• Identify and communicate Overtime needs.  When applicable, acquire overtime help and accurately apply overtime guidelines; ensure correct overtime lists are posted at all times.

• Lead employee disciplinary investigation and action as appropriate. Partner with HR to conduct timely investigations when necessary. Complete accurate and thorough disciplinary records with supporting documentation.

• Ensure attendance discipline is issued in a timely manner and consistent with the Attendance Policy.

• Distribute written communications in a timely fashion.

QUALITY:  Ensure the product produced on manufacturing line is defect-free and produced according to specification.

• Ensure all quality processes/standards are followed within assigned production area.

• Monitor quality issues on a daily basis and drives the resolution or escalation for any defect.

• Ensure Team Leaders include quality standards in Standardized Work to meet design intent and build in quality.

• Work cross-functionally with multiple stakeholders to address and solve production line quality issues (i.e. Team Leader, engineering, quality).

• Monitor scrap data/reports to drive resolution of scrap issues and work projects to prevent future scrap.

• Partner with Plant Quality and Engineering staff to drive improvements in First Pass Yield and Service Call Rate (SCR) metrics.

SAFETY:  Responsible for the safety performance and metrics for the production area.

• Promote safety culture and ensure team’s compliance with safety rules and procedures, such as: PPE compliance, accident investigation within 24 hours, Safety Contacts and safe start participation.

• Lead and own accident investigation process to identify root cause and drive required corrective action(s). Log and close accident investigations in a timely manner.

• Manage the department's safety action item list, including corrective actions from near misses, accident reports & ergo assessments.

What You'll Bring to Our Team

• Leadership experience and/or technical acumen within supply chain (ie: manufacturing, warehousing, distribution, materials, quality, procurement, fulfillment or related functional area).

• BS/BA degree, ideally in engineering, supply chain management or business.

• 5 years of leadership experience in a manufacturing environment, supplier management and project implementation.

• Six Sigma certification preferred, with strong knowledge of Lean, DMAIC, workout and other change mechanisms.

• Demonstrated accomplishments showing results-driven methodology, analytical methods, schedule achievement, team work.

• Lean Manufacturing implementation experience.

• Strong verbal and written communication, interpersonal and leadership influencing skills.

Working Conditions:

• Working conditions are normal for both an office and manufacturing environment.

• Work may involve lifting of materials and product up to 25 pounds.

• Working in the manufacturing environment requires the use of safety equipment to include but not limited to: safety glasses, hearing protection, gloves, work shoes/boots.

Our Culture

Our work is centered on our People and Culture as reflected in our Zero Distance philosophy and we recognize the importance of reaffirming our commitment to inclusion and diversity (I&D). This underscores our commitment to fostering an environment where every individual feels valued, connected, and empowered to contribute, while positioning our organization to adapt seamlessly to the evolving needs of our workforce and communities.

This reflects our dedication to creating solutions that: Empower colleagues by fostering an environment where all voices are heard, valued, and encouraged to contribute. Strengthen communities where we live and work. Reinforce a culture of belonging, purpose, and engagement. Reflect the diversity of the communities we serve through our workforce, products, and practices.

By further embedding Zero Distance into our People and Culture framework, we will continue to build a deeply connected organization. We are cultivating a culture of engagement, belonging, and connection, because while attracting new talent remains a priority, retention is a cornerstone of our strategy.

GE Appliances is a trust-based organization. It is important we offer our employees the flexibility they need to do their best work while balancing the needs of the business and individuals. When you join GE Appliances, you will have the opportunity to work with your leader to create a flexible work arrangement that balances the needs of the individual, team, and organization.

GE Appliances is an Equal Opportunity Employer.  Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

Senior Manager, Materials - 3rd Shift

Location
USA, Decatur, AL

The Principal Advanced Manufacturing Engineer (AME) is a member of a product line AME team responsible for providing manufacturing support New Product Introduction (NPI), Cost-Out and Plant Productivity projects. The AME shall develop, manage and execute capital equipment and high-volume manufacturing process projects to meet the required budget and launch schedules. The AME is a key liaison between NPI programs and the factory operations teams; ensuring plant priorities and objectives are clearly understood and considered. This includes providing input for design for manufacturability, applying lean principles to process designs and transferring process knowledge to the applicable factory personnel. The role requires strong experience with manufacturing equipment and automation systems used in high-volume production environments as well as Openness to leveraging AI-assisted tools and technologies to support technical documentation creation, review, process standardization, and knowledge management activities.

Position
Principal Advanced Manufacturing Engineer

Location
USA, Decatur, AL

How You'll Create Possibilities

Technical Responsibilities:

• Coordinate and manage capital equipment procurement projects: Including specification development utilizing GE Appliances & industry standards, supplier selection, early supplier engagement, technical reviews, factory layout development, installation and qualification of equipment.

• Ensure all tooling and equipment is reliable and robust and designed to maximize Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE).

• Own the program metrics as applicable to your assigned projects: capital equipment & tooling budgets, program schedule, reliability, quality and labor targets.

• Work with the program team to perform trade-off analysis on competing metrics if necessary and drive decisions based on overall business impact.

• Facilitate/lead the use of the Production Preparation Process (3P) and Lean manufacturing principles while developing manufacturing equipment and processes.

• Utilize cross-functional participation to ensure that the equipment and processes are compatible with the entire value stream.  Efforts should include right-sized equipment, workstation design, material presentation, standard work and single piece flow.

• Ensure all equipment executed in GEA factories comply with Industry and Governmental Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) standards.

• Utilize Human Organizational Performance (HOP) principles to ensure that all equipment / tooling / processes are implemented with the health and safety of the operators in mind.

• Work with functional leaders to ensure equipment & processes support business initiatives of Bill of Process (BoP), Lean Manufacturing, Ergonomic Design and Total Productive Maintenance (TPM)

Cross-functional Work and Leadership:

• Work with factory operations and Lean teams to understand Value Stream and how your projects impact this.  Ensure material flow, workstation setup, model mix, etc. are considered when workstations/equipment is designed.

• Work with the design team to ensure Design for Manufacturing & Assembly (DFMA) is considered part design.

Guides technical support & troubleshooting process issues and drives operational improvements, through effective problem solving and corrective action implementation, to continuously improve safety, quality, delivery, cost & morale.

Position
Senior Process Improvement Engineer

Location
USA, Decatur, AL

How You'll Create Possibilities

EQUIPMENT:

• Own all equipment and tooling in the production area, from Engineering sign-off and forward.

• Serve as the primary troubleshooting resource for the process in the plant. Consult with maintenance staff on equipment repair.

• Monitor and work to improve Overall Equipment Efficiency (OEE) in the area.

• Recommend equipment and tooling for existing process; consult and sign-off on new purchases when applicable.

• Responsible for and lead corrective action for Preventative Maintenance plans to ensure compliance and maximize equipment uptime.

• Own Total Preventive Maintenance activities for the area.

• Consult with Maintenance Business Leader on the maintenance action item list and/or priorities for the area.

• Provide feedback on equipment specifications based upon GE Appliances equipment standard and lessons learned.

SAFETY:

• Support Business Leader by identifying and implementing safety-related corrective actions and improvements for the area.

• Assist with action item completion for the area's safety action item list, including corrective actions from near misses, accident reports & ergo assessments.

• Update any inefficiencies in lock out tag out (LOTO) and attend annual training sessions.

PROCESS CONTROL:

• Active participant in the development of the Manufacturing Control Plan and ensure it is adhered to within the production area.

• Maintain process-level standards/procedures.

• Work cross-functionally with multiple stakeholders to quickly address, identify root cause and solve production line issues (i.e. Operations, Safety, Quality).

CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT:

• Engage in and lead problem-solving for production area. Lead root cause identification of problems, implement appropriate countermeasures, and share across as best practice.

• Support the Team and Business Leaders in the planning and execution of continuous improvement method.

NPI LAUNCHES:

• Coordinate with Engineers on equipment purchases & qualification.

• Interact with Design Engineers/Technology organization on model changes for manufacturing line set up.

• Review product prototypes and concepts for manufacturability.

• Provide feedback to the NPI team on capacity, impact on operator and process stability/sustainability.

What You'll Bring to Our Team

• Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering or technical field, or equivalent education & experience.

• Minimum of 3 years’ experience in Manufacturing Engineering/Operations/Quality support roles or equivalent military experience.

• Strong verbal & written communication skills coupled with interpersonal skills.

• Advanced computer skills - high proficiency in Microsoft products with the ability to grasp new systems quickly.

• Strong project management with high analytical and problem-solving skills
